prompt: A battalion WARNO arrives at D-1 1000H and the defense must be prepared by 0400H on D. Using the one-third/two-thirds guideline, by what time must the company OPORD be issued at the latest?
explanation: The timeline is 18 hours, so the company keeps 6 hours: the OPORD is NLT 1600H (planned 1500H) and subordinates keep the rest.

prompt: A company plans forward from receipt of the mission and finds no time left to rehearse before the battalion rehearsal. Which sample practice prevents this?
options: Issuing the WARNO only after the tentative plan is complete and approved
Keeping one-half of the time for the company's own planning and orders
Starting the timeline from the time the company OPORD is issued to subordinates
Reverse-planning from the "defense prepared" time with battalion deadlines
explanation: The sample timeline is reverse-planned from 0400H and includes the battalion's backbrief, rehearsal and evacuation deadlines.

prompt: A company commander holds the WARNO until the plan is finished, so subordinates wait. Which "why this works" point of the sample WARNO is lost?
options: It names the place of the OPORD on the ground overlooking the EA
It gives the OP task early so that the squad can plan its move
Out fast, so subordinates can start moving and preparing at once
It is reverse-planned from the battalion defense-prepared time
explanation: The study notes say the WARNO works because it goes out fast; the sample issues it 15 minutes after the battalion WARNO.

prompt: Which statement matches the sample timeline for the company on D-1?
options: It issues the OPORD at 1500H and moves only after the order is out
It moves at 1300H, before the OPORD at 1500H, to use time on the ground
It moves at 1500H at BP2 together with the issue of the OPORD
It moves after the stand-to so that the plan is already final
explanation: The company moves to its sector at 1300H, before its order is issued, because waiting for a finished plan before moving is the mistake to avoid.

prompt: Route 7 must stay open until 2000, and the R1 obstacle may be closed only on battalion order. How does the sample mission analysis classify these items?
options: Specified tasks
Implied tasks
Essential tasks
Constraints
explanation: Both are limits on when and how the company may act, which the sample lists under constraints.

prompt: In the sample war-game, the enemy mortars the company's emitters. Which counteraction does the plan list?
options: Remote antennas and use wire
Use 90RR and BC2001
Use BP1 and BC2002
Use camouflage and emission control
explanation: The war-game pairs each enemy event with a counteraction: mortars on emitters is answered by remote antennas and wire, while the drone at BMNT is answered by camouflage and emission control.

prompt: In COA 1, which element's task and purpose is to destroy the creek element so it cannot flank the main effort?
options: 2nd PLT (ME) with the 90RR at BP2
3rd PLT(-) (SE2) at BP3
1st PLT (SE1) at BP1
The OP squad on Hill 310
explanation: SE1 at BP1 destroys the creek element so it cannot flank the ME. SE2 at BP3 blocks penetration of PL STEEL.

prompt: Which list gives the factors on the sample war-game decision matrix?
options: Depth, mass at the EA, creek coverage, simplicity, obstacle integration, survivability
Depth, mass at the EA, creek coverage, speed, obstacle integration, survivability
Depth, mass at the EA, creek coverage, simplicity, obstacle integration, supportability
Depth, dispersion, creek coverage, simplicity, obstacle integration, survivability
explanation: The matrix compares COA 1 and COA 2 on six factors; the study notes warn against factors unrelated to the war-game.

prompt: The platoon leader needs to know the distance at which the cane stops hiding the enemy. Which sample recon task answers this gap?
options: Pace from PL IRON to the cane edge (2nd PL)
Walk the creek from the enemy side (1st PL)
Walk the positions and mark limits (CO and PLs)
Recon the R1 site and bypasses (engineer squad leader)
explanation: The sample answers the engagement distance gap by pacing from PL IRON to the cane edge, assigned to the 2nd PL.

prompt: In the sample reconnaissance table, who confirms the R1 site and bypasses, and when?
options: The OP squad leader, 1600H
The engineer squad leader, 1430H
The 1st PLT leader, 1100H
The commander and platoon leaders, 1030H
explanation: Each gap names who confirms it and when: Engr SL at 1430H for R1, and OP SL at 1600H for the OP site and withdrawal route.

prompt: Which pair of movements matches the sample?
options: The company moves at 1030H; the OP moves at 1930H to be in place by 2000H
The company moves at 1300H; the OP moves at 1930H to be in place by 2000H
The company moves at 1300H; the OP moves at 1600H to be in place by 1700H
The company moves at 1500H; the OP moves at 1300H to be in place by 1500H
explanation: The slide closes Step 4 with the company moving at 1300H and the OP moving at 1930H to be in place by 2000H.

prompt: How does Step 5 reconnaissance in the sample defense differ from the attack in the comparison table?
options: The leader looks at the engagement area from our own side instead of from the enemy's side during the recon
The leader waits for the OPORD before any recon of the sector instead of moving early
The leader walks the engagement area from the enemy's side instead of looking at the objective from our side
The leader leaves the whole sector recon to the engineer squad leader alone
explanation: In the attack the leader looks at the objective from our side; in the defense the leader walks the engagement area from the enemy's side.

prompt: A group lists company VHF as its primary means, although the OPFOR has already mortared emitters. Which change follows the sample?
options: Keep VHF primary and add a second company radio net as a back-up
Make messengers primary and drop the wire from the plan altogether
Copy the battalion CEOI into paragraph 5 as the company plan
Make field wire primary and remote the antennas
explanation: The sample warns against radio as primary when the enemy hunts emitters: wire is primary and antennas are remoted.

prompt: Which list gives the sample PACE plan from primary to emergency?
options: Company VHF B2; field wire to BPs; messengers; pyro or whistle
Field wire to BPs; company VHF B2; messengers; pyro or whistle
Field wire to BPs; messengers; company VHF B2; pyro or whistle
Field wire to BPs; company VHF B2; pyro or whistle; messengers
explanation: The plan is P: field wire to BPs, A: company VHF B2, C: messengers, E: pyro and whistle.

prompt: Which of the following is named as the mistake to AVOID in paragraph 5 of the sample order?
options: Making field wire the primary means in the defense
Remoting the antennas
Copying the battalion CEOI as paragraph 5
Planning a KIDLAT drill for the whole company
explanation: The other three are parts of the sample's company plan. Copying the battalion CEOI is the mistake to avoid.

prompt: According to the study notes, what should paragraph 5 of the company order be?
options: A copy of the battalion CEOI with the company callsigns added
A list of every radio net used across the whole battalion
A timeline of the battalion rehearsals and backbriefs
A real company plan matched to the enemy's DF threat
explanation: The notes say paragraph 5 is a real company plan matched to the enemy's DF threat, which is where signal officers show their value.

prompt: During PCIs the wire to BP2 is found cut, and the company switches to company VHF B2. Which PACE level is now in use?
options: Alternate
Primary
Contingency
Emergency
explanation: Field wire is the primary means, so company VHF B2 is the alternate.

prompt: Which pair of Step 8 activities serves these purposes in order: "check mutual support and gaps" and "check from the enemy's side"?
options: The rock drill and fires support rehearsal; stand-to through BMNT
Platoon leader backbriefs; the commander walks the line
PCIs and wire and radio checks; the commander walks the line
Platoon leader backbriefs with sector sketches; stand-to through BMNT
explanation: The Step 8 table pairs backbriefs with mutual support and gaps, and the commander's walk of the line with the enemy's-side check.

prompt: A group's Step 8 says only "we will rehearse." What does the sample add?
options: A list of the priorities of work in order, from security to dig
Leaders checking the positions themselves before the attack
The rehearsal type and method, focused on critical events
The PACE plan with the stand-to time for the company
explanation: The study notes say the rehearsal names its type and method and focuses on critical events; "we will rehearse" with no type or focus is the example to avoid.

prompt: How does Step 8 differ between the sample defense and an attack in the comparison table?
options: The defense rehearses the assault at the attack position; the attack checks positions, fields of fire and wire
The defense moves to the attack position; the attack stands to at BMNT
The defense walks the objective; the attack walks the engagement area
The defense checks positions, fields of fire and wire and stands to at BMNT; the attack rehearses the assault
explanation: The table gives "check positions, fields of fire and wire; rehearse the fight; stand-to at BMNT" for the defense and "rehearse the assault" for the attack.
